subject: business-studies
title: IRR and Choosing a Method
welcome_lead: IRR finds the break-even discount rate - and each method has its uses.
meta_desc: A-Level Investment Appraisal: IRR and method choice.
final_note: Use multiple methods - they give different answers for a reason.

concepts.def: Discount rate at which NPV equals zero.
Accept if IRR exceeds the cost of capital.
Choosing between projects where only one can run.
How NPV changes if assumptions vary.
Non-financial issues such as fit, ethics, brand.

walkthroughs.body_html: IRR is the discount rate that makes NPV zero. If IRR exceeds the firm's cost of capital, the project earns more than the funds raised cost - accept it.
For independent projects NPV and IRR agree. For mutually exclusive projects of different scale they may conflict - most theorists favour NPV as the safer rule.
Even strong NPV projects can be rejected for strategic, ethical or reputational reasons. The quantitative tools must feed into wider judgment.

Break-even is where the business makes the most profit.
Break-even is where the business owes no debt.
The level of output where total revenue equals total costs — neither profit nor loss. It is NOT the level where profit is maximised; profit grows beyond break-even.

options: Taylor invented the assembly line at Ford.

Workers are motivated primarily by money; efficiency is maximised by breaking tasks into standardised steps, training workers in 'the one best way', and using piece-rate pay.

Cost advantages a firm gains as it grows — average cost per unit falls because fixed costs spread over more units, bulk discounts, and specialisation become possible.
